    "# Tutorial: fmdtools basics"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "raw",
   "id": "2f24c001",
   "metadata": {

   },

    "\n",
    "## Overview\n",
    "This tutorial shows the basics of:\n",
    "\n",
    "1. working with fmdtools to model a system (in this example, a multirotor drone with a few variants), \n",
    "\n",
    "2. simulating a model in nominal and hazardous scenarios, and\n",
    "\n",
    "3. analyzing and visualizing the results of simulations. "
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c99499af",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Multorotor Drone folder\n",
    "\n",
    "The `multirotor_drone` folder has a few different models that are meant to represent **different types of models** that can be built in fmdtools (in terms of fidelity) and showcase how **more detailed models** can be built from **less detailed models.**\n",
    "\n",
    "The models in this folder include:\n",
    "\n",
    "- `model_static.py`: a multirotor drone simulated at a single timestep with very basic abstract behaviors to capture failure propagation in a \"static flight\" case\n",
    "\n",
    "- `model_dynamic.py`: an extended version of this drone with dynamic behaviors (e.g., basic flight dynamics, battery usage, etc.)\n",
    "\n",
    "- `model_hierarchical.py`: a version with multiple component architectures embodying the \"StoreEE\" (battery architecture) and \"AffectDOF\" (line/rotor architecture) functions\n",
    "\n",
    "- `model_rural.py`: a version that flies in a rural scenario (viewing the area in a field)\n",
    "\n",
    "- `model_urban.py`: a version that over buildings in an urban setting "
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "fec962f8",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Multirotor Drone Structure \n",
    "\n",
    "Models in fmdtools can take many different forms, depending on the use-case. When we want to model how different behaviors of a system interact, we often represent the system as a `FunctionArchitecture` that is made up of `Function` objects that are connected with each other via `Flow` objects.\n",
    "\n",
    "## Drone Functions\n",
    "\n",
    "- `store_ee`: Store the electrical energy that powers the system (e.g., batteries)\n",
    "\n",
    "- `dist_ee`: Distribute the electrical energy that powers the system (e.g., wiring and circuitry)\n",
    "\n",
    "- `affect_dof`: Modify the position and velocity of the system (e.g., rotor architecture)\n",
    "\n",
    "- `ctl_dof`: Control the position and velocity of the system to its desired state (e.g., control system)\n",
    "\n",
    "- `plan_path`: Plan the desired trajectory of the drone and produce the neccesary controls (e.g., navigation)\n",
    "\n",
    "- `hold_payload`: Structurally support the weight of the drone and its payloads (e.g., structures)\n",
    "\n",
    "- `view_env`: View the environment (e.g., camera)\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "## Drone Flows\n",
    "\n",
    "- `force_st`: Force connecting the body of the drone with the ground\n",
    "\n",
    "- `force_lin`: Force connecting the rotors with the body of the drone\n",
    "\n",
    "- `ee_1`: Electricity out of the battery (to be distributed)\n",
    "\n",
    "- `ee_mot`: Electricity to the motors\n",
    "\n",
    "- `ee_ctl`: Electricity to the electronics\n",
    "\n",
    "- `ctl`: Control signals to the motors\n",
    "\n",
    "- `dofs`: Degrees of freedom (trajectory, velocity) of the drone\n",
    "\n",
    "- `des_traj`: Desired trajectory of the drone\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "ce3f85b6",
   "metadata": {
    "vscode": {
     "languageId": "raw"
    }
   },
   "source": [
    "## Drone model file\n",
    "\n",
    "To get an idea of what a model file looks like (as well as the different pieces), look through `model_static.py`. Here we import this model to look at its structure:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 15,
   "id": "0aa98086",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "class Drone(FunctionArchitecture):\n",
      "    \"\"\"Static multirotor drone model (executes in a single timestep).\"\"\"\n",
      "\n",
      "    default_sp = {'end_time': 0}\n",
      "\n",
      "    def init_architecture(self, **kwargs):\n",
      "        # add flows to the model\n",
      "        self.add_flow(\"force_st\", Force)\n",
      "        self.add_flow(\"force_lin\", Force)\n",
      "        self.add_flow(\"ee_1\", EE)\n",
      "        self.add_flow(\"ee_mot\", EE)\n",
      "        self.add_flow(\"ee_ctl\", EE)\n",
      "        self.add_flow(\"ctl\", Control)\n",
      "        self.add_flow(\"dofs\", DOFs)\n",
      "        self.add_flow(\"des_traj\", DesTraj)\n",
      "        # add functions to the model\n",
      "        self.add_fxn(\"store_ee\", StoreEE, \"ee_1\", \"force_st\")\n",
      "        self.add_fxn(\"dist_ee\", DistEE, \"ee_1\", \"ee_mot\", \"ee_ctl\", \"force_st\")\n",
      "        self.add_fxn(\"affect_dof\", AffectDOF, \"ee_mot\", \"ctl\", \"dofs\", \"force_lin\")\n",
      "        self.add_fxn(\"ctl_dof\", CtlDOF, \"ee_ctl\", \"des_traj\", \"ctl\", \"dofs\", \"force_st\")\n",
      "        self.add_fxn(\"plan_path\", PlanPath, \"ee_ctl\", \"des_traj\", \"force_st\", \"dofs\")\n",
      "        self.add_fxn(\"hold_payload\", HoldPayload, \"dofs\", \"force_lin\", \"force_st\")\n",
      "        self.add_fxn(\"view_env\", ViewEnvironment, \"dofs\")\n",
      "\n",
      "    def classify(self, scen={}, mdlhist={}, **kwargs):\n",
      "        \"\"\"Calculate rate, cost, expected cost based on cost of repair information.\"\"\"\n",
      "        modeprops = self.return_faultmodes()\n",
      "        repcost = sum([m[\"cost\"] for f, m in modeprops.items()])\n",
      "\n",
      "        totcost = repcost\n",
      "        rate = scen.rate\n",
      "        expcost = totcost * rate * 1e5\n",
      "        return {\"rate\": rate, \"cost\": totcost, \"expected_cost\": expcost}\n",
      "\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "import inspect\n",
    "from fmdtools_examples.multirotor_drone.model_static import Drone, EE, StoreEE\n",
    "print(inspect.getsource(Drone))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f3c72da6",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Drone Architecture\n",
    "\n",
    "To instantiate the model, you can use:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 16,
   "id": "53710da3",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "drone Drone\n",
       "- t=Time(time=-0.1, timers={})\n",
       "- m=Mode(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False)\n",
       "FLOWS:\n",
       "- force_st=Force(s=(support=1.0))\n",
       "- force_lin=Force(s=(support=1.0))\n",
       "- ee_1=EE(s=(rate=1.0, effort=1.0))\n",
       "- ee_mot=EE(s=(rate=1.0, effort=1.0))\n",
       "- ee_ctl=EE(s=(rate=1.0, effort=1.0))\n",
       "- ctl=Control(s=(forward=1.0, upward=1.0))\n",
       "- dofs=DOFs(s=(vertvel=1.0, planvel=1.0, planpwr=1.0, uppwr=1.0, x=0.0, y=0.0, z=0.0))\n",
       "- des_traj=DesTraj(s=(dx=1.0, dy=0.0, dz=0.0, power=1.0))\n",
       "FXNS:\n",
       "- store_ee=StoreEE(s=(soc=100.0), m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- dist_ee=DistEE(s=(ee_tr=1.0, ee_te=1.0), m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- affect_dof=AffectDOF(s=(e_to=1.0, e_ti=1.0, ct=1.0, mt=1.0, pt=1.0), m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- ctl_dof=CtlDOF(s=(cs=1.0, power=1.0), m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- plan_path=PlanPath(m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- hold_payload=HoldPayload(s=(force_gr=1.0), m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- view_env=ViewEnvironment(m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 16,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mdl = Drone()\n",
    "mdl"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "3629ccd9",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b993832f",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "As shown, each function has its connected flows as a part of its definition.\n",
    "\n",
    "The result is a graph of behaviors (functions) that interact via shared variables (flows)  \n",
    "\n",
    "Note that some of the flow names appear different at the function level than the architecture level. This is because they have been given local flow names."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 20,
   "id": "420182e8",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "store_ee StoreEE\n",
       "- t=Time(time=-0.1, timers={})\n",
       "- s=StoreEEState(soc=100.0)\n",
       "- m=StoreEEMode(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False)\n",
       "- ee_out=EE(s=(rate=1.0, effort=1.0))\n",
       "- fs=Force(s=(support=1.0))"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 20,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mdl.fxns['store_ee'] # see flow \"fs\" - at the architecture level this was force_st!"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 21,
   "id": "7d5d1f30",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "force_st Force\n",
       "- s=ForceState(support=1.0)"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 21,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mdl.fxns['store_ee'].fs # while the local variable name is fs, it is still the force_st that we want (that connects other pieces)"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "## Viewing the drone architecture\n",
    "\n",
    "The behavioral interactions between functions via flows can be visualized as a graph:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 23,
   "id": "dd5dabda",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 1200x1000 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mg = mdl.as_modelgraph()\n",
    "fig, ax = mg.draw()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "bdab2b87",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "This graph is often pretty ugly by default because the layout is auto-generated via an algorithm in the `networkx` package"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d2b138f1",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Making the graph pretty(er)\n",
    "\n",
    "The outputted \"Model Graph\" is an [Graph](https://nasa.github.io/fmdtools/docs-source/fmdtools.analyze.graph.html#fmdtools-analyze-graph-base) class (which heavily uses the `networkx` library), which has built-in options for applying different styles and moving nodes."
   ]
  },

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "da661baa",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "More info on working with graphs can be found in [Tutorial: Model Structure Visualization](https://nasa.github.io/fmdtools/examples/navigating_rover/tutorial_model_structure_visualization.html)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "eb3f4237",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Simulation\n",
    "\n",
    "There are several ways to simulate fmdtools models. One of the most flexible is to use the model directly:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 27,
   "id": "37683da9",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "drone Drone\n",
       "- t=Time(time=0.0, timers={})\n",
       "- m=Mode(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False)\n",
       "FLOWS:\n",
       "- force_st=Force(s=(support=1.0))\n",
       "- force_lin=Force(s=(support=1.0))\n",
       "- ee_1=EE(s=(rate=1.0, effort=1.0))\n",
       "- ee_mot=EE(s=(rate=1.0, effort=1.0))\n",
       "- ee_ctl=EE(s=(rate=1.0, effort=1.0))\n",
       "- ctl=Control(s=(forward=1.0, upward=1.0))\n",
       "- dofs=DOFs(s=(vertvel=0.0, planvel=1.0, planpwr=1.0, uppwr=1.0, x=0.0, y=0.0, z=1.0))\n",
       "- des_traj=DesTraj(s=(dx=1.0, dy=0.0, dz=0.0, power=1.0))\n",
       "FXNS:\n",
       "- store_ee=StoreEE(s=(soc=100.0), m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- dist_ee=DistEE(s=(ee_tr=1.0, ee_te=1.0), m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- affect_dof=AffectDOF(s=(e_to=1.0, e_ti=1.0, ct=1.0, mt=1.0, pt=1.0), m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- ctl_dof=CtlDOF(s=(cs=1.0, power=1.0), m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- plan_path=PlanPath(m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- hold_payload=HoldPayload(s=(force_gr=0.0), m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))\n",
       "- view_env=ViewEnvironment(m=(mode='nominal', faults=set(), sub_faults=False))"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 27,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mdl(0)\n",
    "mdl"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b2342c93",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Note the change in state in the system--most notably the incremented timestep (now 1).\n",
    "\n",
    "## Simulation Limitation\n",
    "\n",
    "Since this model is only meant to run one timestep, simulating further gives us an error:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 28,
   "id": "d1770686",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# mdl()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "ab635787",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Simulation Parameter and History\n",
    "\n",
    "Models can be run to different times depending on their Simulation Parameter (see: [SimParam](https://nasa.github.io/fmdtools/docs-source/fmdtools.define.block.html#fmdtools.define.block.base.SimParam). The static model, by default, only simulates one timestep at `t=0`:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 29,
   "id": "aaf012d9",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "SimParam(phases=(('na', 0.0, 0),), start_time=0.0, end_time=0.0, track_times=('all',), dt=1.0, units='hr', end_condition='', use_local=True, with_loadings=False, run_stochastic=False, track_pdf=False)"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 29,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mdl.sp # simulation parameter"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9fc10474",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "This parameter can be changed at model instantiation and sets the end condition (in this case, `end_time`), which in turn determines how long the simulation will run and how long the history is. See:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 30,
   "id": "423c1e36",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "time:                           array(3)\n",
       "flows.force_st.s.support:       array(3)\n",
       "flows.force_lin.s.support:      array(3)\n",
       "flows.ee_1.s.rate:              array(3)\n",
       "flows.ee_1.s.effort:            array(3)\n",
       "flows.ee_mot.s.rate:            array(3)\n",
       "flows.ee_mot.s.effort:          array(3)\n",
       "flows.ee_ctl.s.rate:            array(3)\n",
       "flows.ee_ctl.s.effort:          array(3)\n",
       "flows.ctl.s.forward:            array(3)\n",
       "flows.ctl.s.upward:             array(3)\n",
       "flows.dofs.s.vertvel:           array(3)\n",
       "flows.dofs.s.planvel:           array(3)\n",
       "flows.dofs.s.planpwr:           array(3)\n",
       "flows.dofs.s.uppwr:             array(3)\n",
       "flows.dofs.s.x:                 array(3)\n",
       "flows.dofs.s.y:                 array(3)\n",
       "flows.dofs.s.z:                 array(3)\n",
       "flows.des_traj.s.dx:            array(3)\n",
       "flows.des_traj.s.dy:            array(3)\n",
       "flows.des_traj.s.dz:            array(3)\n",
       "flows.des_traj.s.power:         array(3)\n",
       "fxns.store_ee.s.soc:            array(3)\n",
       "fxns.store_ee.m.faults.nocharge: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.store_ee.m.sub_faults:     array(3)\n",
       "fxns.dist_ee.s.ee_tr:           array(3)\n",
       "fxns.dist_ee.s.ee_te:           array(3)\n",
       "fxns.dist_ee.m.faults.break:    array(3)\n",
       "fxns.dist_ee.m.faults.degr:     array(3)\n",
       "fxns.dist_ee.m.faults.short:    array(3)\n",
       "fxns.dist_ee.m.sub_faults:      array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.s.e_to:         array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.s.e_ti:         array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.s.ct:           array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.s.mt:           array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.s.pt:           array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.m.faults.ctlbreak: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.m.faults.ctldn: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.m.faults.ctlup: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.m.faults.mechbreak: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.m.faults.mechfriction: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.m.faults.openc: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.m.faults.propbreak: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.m.faults.propstuck: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.m.faults.propwarp: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.m.faults.short: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.affect_dof.m.sub_faults:   array(3)\n",
       "fxns.ctl_dof.s.cs:              array(3)\n",
       "fxns.ctl_dof.s.power:           array(3)\n",
       "fxns.ctl_dof.m.faults.degctl:   array(3)\n",
       "fxns.ctl_dof.m.faults.noctl:    array(3)\n",
       "fxns.ctl_dof.m.sub_faults:      array(3)\n",
       "fxns.plan_path.m.faults.degloc: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.plan_path.m.faults.noloc:  array(3)\n",
       "fxns.plan_path.m.sub_faults:    array(3)\n",
       "fxns.hold_payload.s.force_gr:   array(3)\n",
       "fxns.hold_payload.m.faults.break: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.hold_payload.m.faults.deform: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.hold_payload.m.sub_faults: array(3)\n",
       "fxns.view_env.m.sub_faults:     array(3)"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 30,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mdl = Drone(sp={'end_time': 2})\n",
    "mdl.h"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "3eb29b9e",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Simulation: A more interesting case\n",
    "\n",
    "To better showcase simulation, we are going to use the model in `model_dynamic.py`\n",
    "\n",
    "This model builds on the architecture of the Drone model in `model_static.py` but adds behaviors that increment over time, meaning we can look at the behavior over multiple timesteps."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 31,
   "id": "cd8bd59c",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "SimParam(phases=(('ascend', 0, 1), ('forward', 2, 14), ('descend', 15, 18), ('taxi', 19, 20)), start_time=0.0, end_time=20.0, track_times=('all',), dt=1.0, units='sec', end_condition='', use_local=True, with_loadings=False, run_stochastic=False, track_pdf=False)"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 31,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "from model_dynamic import Drone\n",
    "\n",
    "mdl = Drone()\n",
    "mdl.sp"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "5fedf234",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "A single timestep simulates via:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 32,
   "id": "6ddd0580",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "Time(time=1.0, t_ind=1, timers={}, use_local=True, dt=1.0, executed_static=True, executed_dynamic=True, executing=False)"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 32,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mdl()\n",
    "mdl.t"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2ee92324",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Or, to a given time-step:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 33,
   "id": "bb125a75",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "mdl(time=20.0)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 34,
   "id": "69a75a6c",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "Time(time=20.0, t_ind=20, timers={}, use_local=True, dt=1.0, executed_static=True, executed_dynamic=True, executing=False)"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 34,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mdl.t"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "4b7d1d9e",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Examining Simulation States\n",
    "\n",
    "Given we've simulated the model to a given time-step, we can examine the states of the system and its history to see what happened:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 35,
   "id": "1057e5f8",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "StoreEEState(soc=89.5)"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 35,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mdl.fxns['store_ee'].s"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 36,
   "id": "a57724cf",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "array([99.5, 99. , 98.5, 98. , 97.5, 97. , 96.5, 96. , 95.5, 95. , 94.5,\n",
       "       94. , 93.5, 93. , 92.5, 92. , 91.5, 91. , 90.5, 90. , 89.5])"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 36,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "mdl.h.fxns.store_ee.s.soc"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "21c6115a",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The `classify` method defined in the Model can also be used to classify the results of a given scenario."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 37,
   "id": "b4f79065",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "{'rate': 1.0, 'cost': 0, 'expected_cost': 0.0, 'lost_cost': 0, 'crashcost': 0}"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 37,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "from fmdtools.sim.scenario import Scenario\n",
    "mdl.classify(scen=Scenario())"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f8ca6b4b",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "We might want to be able to know more about the states of the system as a whole! We'll cover more of that in the analysis portion of the tutorial."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "16c2b698",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Using the `sim.propagate` module\n",
    "\n",
    "While you can always simulate models directly, `sim.propagate` has a lot of functionality that makes it easier to simulate scenarios of interest."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 38,
   "id": "fd8f3709",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from fmdtools.sim import propagate"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e31c75d5",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The simplest is `propagate.nominal`, which simulates the nominal scenario. Propagate methods return `Result` and `History` objects, like so:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 39,
   "id": "f99c78a7",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "tend.classify.rate:                  1.0\n",
       "tend.classify.cost:                    0\n",
       "tend.classify.expected_cost:         0.0\n",
       "tend.classify.lost_cost:               0\n",
       "tend.classify.crashcost:               0"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 39,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "res, hist = propagate.nominal(mdl)\n",
    "res"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 40,
   "id": "2093383f",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [

  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "26c014d1",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Verifying nominal outputs\n",
    "\n",
    "With a history, you can use `History.plot_line` to verify that the system progresses through states as expected:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 41,
   "id": "155454e7",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 900x400 with 6 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "fig, axs = hist.plot_line(\"fxns.store_ee.s.soc\", \"fxns.plan_path.m.mode\", \"fxns.plan_path.s.dist\", \"flows.dofs.s.x\", \"flows.dofs.s.y\", \"flows.dofs.s.z\", cols=3)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "5dd839d5",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Verifying nominal trajectories\n",
    "\n",
    "For trajectory information (x, y, and z coordinates), you can use `History.plot_trajectories`, which can work when there are two or three variables to plot:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 42,
   "id": "49499a88",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 400x400 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# fix, ax = hist.plot_trajectories(\"flows.dofs.s.x\", \"flows.dofs.s.y\", \"flows.dofs.s.z\", time_groups=[\"nominal\"], time_ticks=5.0)\n",
    "fix, ax = hist.plot_trajectories(\"flows.dofs.s.x\", \"flows.dofs.s.y\", time_groups=[\"nominal\"], time_ticks=5.0)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "12b3c316",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Simulating a fault scenario\n",
    "\n",
    "We can simulate individual fault scenarios using `propagate.one_fault`. A fault scenario is a combination of a fault mode (defined as `fault_faultname` in a `Mode`) and a time.\n",
    "\n",
    "Here we inject a `nocharge` fault into the `store_ee` function at time `t=10.0`:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 43,
   "id": "1dbbc621",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "tend.classify.rate:                1e-05\n",
       "tend.classify.cost:               183000\n",
       "tend.classify.expected_cost:    183000.0\n",
       "tend.classify.lost_cost:           50000\n",
       "tend.classify.crashcost:          100000"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 43,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "res_lowcharge, hist_lowcharge = propagate.one_fault(mdl, \"store_ee\", \"nocharge\", 10.0)\n",
    "res_lowcharge.faulty"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "6103671c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "As shown, this causes a crash since the drone can no longer keep itself in the air:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 44,
   "id": "0868428e",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",

      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "fig, ax = hist_lowcharge.plot_trajectories(\"flows.dofs.s.x\", \"flows.dofs.s.y\", \"flows.dofs.s.z\", time_groups=[\"nominal\"], time_ticks=5.0)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c70eaedd",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Examining fault scenario results\n",
    "\n",
    "When simulating scenarios, the returned `Result` and `History` objects include both nominal and faulty scenario information by default. This makes it easier to see what went wrong in a scenario, visualize scenarios and quantify metrics:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 45,
   "id": "0ff5155b",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "nominal: \n",
       "--tend: \n",
       "----classify: \n",
       "------rate:                          1.0\n",
       "------cost:                            0\n",
       "------expected_cost:                 0.0\n",
       "------lost_cost:                       0\n",
       "------crashcost:                       0\n",
       "store_ee_nocharge_t10p0: \n",
       "--tend: \n",
       "----classify: \n",
       "------rate:                        1e-05\n",
       "------cost:                       183000\n",
       "------expected_cost:            183000.0\n",
       "------lost_cost:                   50000\n",
       "------crashcost:                  100000"
      ]
     },

     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],

  },

   "id": "55abb930",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## More on single-scenario simulation\n",
    "\n",
    "Simulation often can mean more than just simulating a fault, but can also include external disturbances or parameters. It may be helpful to familiarize yourself with the following methods:\n",
    "\n",
    "- `propagate.sequence` method: can be used to inject an arbitrary sequence of disturbances and faults in a model and simulate the results\n",
    "\n",
    "- `propagate.Simulation` class: gives more fine-grained control over event simulation, including model copying\n",
    "\n",
    "As well as the options/parameters for these classes and methods."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 76,
   "id": "e2bf9a89",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "<function fmdtools.sim.propagate.sequence(mdl, seq={}, faultseq={}, disturbances={}, scen={}, rate=nan, include_nominal=True, showprogress=False, **kwargs)>"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 76,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "propagate.sequence"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 77,
   "id": "21615c0e",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Help on class Simulation in module fmdtools.sim.propagate:\n",
      "\n",
      "class Simulation(BaseSimulation)\n",
      " |  Simulation(*args, **kwargs)\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  Simulate a single scenario.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  Simulations can be used to do a few things, including:\n",
      " |  (1) Simulating a model in a particular faulty or nominal scenario\n",
      " |  (2) Getting model copies at particular times during a (usually nominal) scenario\n",
      " |  to simulate from. This is helpful for staged simulation where the copies are used\n",
      " |  to simulate faults from the point when the fault occurs instead of simulating\n",
      " |  up to that timestep first\n",
      " |  (3) Generating SampleApproaches that line up with the particular phases of the\n",
      " |  (usually nominal) scenario. This is helpful for nested simulations where each\n",
      " |  set of nominal parameters may change the phases of the simulation and thus the\n",
      " |  fault modes it may enter.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  Parameters\n",
      " |  ----------\n",
      " |  scen : Scenario\n",
      " |      Scenario to simulation\n",
      " |  protect : bool\n",
      " |      Whether to protect the model by re-initializing it.\n",
      " |  copy : bool\n",
      " |      Whether to copy the model prior to simulation\n",
      " |  ctimes : list\n",
      " |      Times to copy the model from during simulation\n",
      " |  simevents : list\n",
      " |      SimEvents to run the system over. Generated from scenario, ctypes, etc.\n",
      " |  warn_faults : bool\n",
      " |      Whether to warn if the simulation is faulty and no faults were injected. Used\n",
      " |      for nominal simulations.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  Examples\n",
      " |  --------\n",
      " |  >>> from fmdtools.define.block.function import ExampleFunction\n",
      " |  >>> sim = Simulation(mdl=ExampleFunction()) # default is nominal simulation\n",
      " |  >>> sim.name\n",
      " |  'nominal'\n",
      " |  >>> sim\n",
      " |  Simulation with SimEvents:\n",
      " |  - end=SimEvent(to_return={'classify': None})\n",
      " |  >>> res, hist = sim()\n",
      " |  >>> res\n",
      " |  tend.classify.xy:                  100.0\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  >>> esf = ExampleFunction() # here we try sometime more complicated:\n",
      " |  >>> s = SingleFaultScenario.from_fault((\"examplefunction\", \"low\"), 3.0, esf)\n",
      " |  >>> sim = Simulation(mdl=esf, scen=s, ctimes = [2, 4], to_return={1.0: 's.x', \"end\": [\"classify\", \"graph\"]})\n",
      " |  >>> sim\n",
      " |  Simulation with SimEvents:\n",
      " |  - 1.0=SimEvent(to_return={'s.x': None})\n",
      " |  - 2.0=SimEvent(copy=True)\n",
      " |  - 3.0=SimEvent(injection=Injection(faults={'examplefunction': ['low']}, disturbances={}))\n",
      " |  - 4.0=SimEvent(copy=True)\n",
      " |  - end=SimEvent(to_return={'classify': None, 'graph': None})\n",
      " |  >>> res, hist = sim()\n",
      " |  >>> sim.mdl\n",
      " |  examplefunction ExampleFunction\n",
      " |  - t=Time(time=100.0, timers={})\n",
      " |  - s=ExampleState(x=20.0, y=294.0)\n",
      " |  - m=ExampleMode(mode='low', faults={'low'}, sub_faults=False)\n",
      " |  - exf=ExampleFlow(s=(x=1964.0, y=1.0))\n",
      " |  >>> [*res.keys()]\n",
      " |  ['t1p0.s.x', 'tend.classify.xy', 'tend.graph']\n",
      " |  >>> sim.get_models()\n",
      " |  {2.0: examplefunction ExampleFunction\n",
      " |  - t=Time(time=1.0, timers={})\n",
      " |  - s=ExampleState(x=1.0, y=0.0)\n",
      " |  - m=ExampleMode(mode='standby', faults=set(), sub_faults=False)\n",
      " |  - exf=ExampleFlow(s=(x=1.0, y=1.0)), 4.0: examplefunction ExampleFunction\n",
      " |  - t=Time(time=3.0, timers={})\n",
      " |  - s=ExampleState(x=20.0, y=3.0)\n",
      " |  - m=ExampleMode(mode='low', faults={'low'}, sub_faults=False)\n",
      " |  - exf=ExampleFlow(s=(x=1.0, y=1.0))}\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  Method resolution order:\n",
      " |      Simulation\n",
      " |      BaseSimulation\n",
      " |      BaseSimContainer\n",
      " |      fmdtools.define.container.base.BaseContainer\n",
      " |      recordclass.datatype.dataobject\n",
      " |      builtins.object\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  Methods defined here:\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __call__(self, with_mdls=False, gen_samp=False, **kwargs)\n",
      " |      Call the sim. Options return copied models and generated sampleapproches.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __init__(self, *args, **kwargs)\n",
      " |      Initialize and create the list of simulation events to run.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __repr__(self)\n",
      " |      Show event sequence in str.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  check_faults(self)\n",
      " |      Check whether there are faults in a nominal simulation (a bad sign).\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  create_simevents(self)\n",
      " |      Create the list of SimEvents to run for during the simulation.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  gen_sampleapproach(self, faultdomains={}, faultsamples={}, get_phasemap=False)\n",
      " |      Generate a SampleApproach from the simulation model.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Parameters\n",
      " |      ----------\n",
      " |      faultdomains : dict, optional\n",
      " |          dict of arguments to add_faultdomains. The default is {}.\n",
      " |      faultsamples : dict, optional\n",
      " |          dict of arguments to add_faultsamples. The default is {}.\n",
      " |      get_phasemap : bool, optional\n",
      " |          Whether to use the history to generate the phasemap used by SampleApproach.\n",
      " |          The default is False.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Returns\n",
      " |      -------\n",
      " |      app : SampleApproach\n",
      " |          Appropriate SampleApproach corresponding to this scenario model/hist\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  get_models(self)\n",
      " |      Get copied models from the simulation.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  init_model(self)\n",
      " |      Initialize the model.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      If self.protect, re-intiates the simulation with scenario parameters.\n",
      " |      If self.copy, copies the simulation.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  run(self, **kwargs)\n",
      " |      Run the simevents and add results to the result dict.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  ----------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
      " |  Data descriptors defined here:\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __dict__\n",
      " |      dictionary for instance variables\n",

      " |  copy\n",

      " |\n",

      " |          Time-range to initialize the history over. The default is None.\n",
      " |      track : list/str/dict, optional\n",
      " |          argument specifying attributes for :func:`get_sub_include'.\n",
      " |          The default is None.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Returns\n",
      " |      -------\n",
      " |      hist : History\n",
      " |          History of fields specified in track.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Examples\n",
      " |      --------\n",
      " |      >>> nest_hist = ExNestContainer().create_hist()\n",
      " |      >>> nest_hist\n",
      " |      e1:\n",
      " |      --x:                            array(1)\n",
      " |      --y:                            array(1)\n",
      " |      z:                              array(1)\n",
      " |      >>> nest_hist.e1.x\n",
      " |      [1.0]\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  create_repr(\n",
      " |      self,\n",
      " |      with_classname=True,\n",
      " |      fields='all',\n",
      " |      one_line=True,\n",
      " |      with_name=False\n",
      " |  )\n",
      " |      Create repr-friendly string for container.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  get_code(self, source)\n",
      " |      Get the code defining the Container.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  get_field_dict(self, obj, *fields, **fielddict)\n",
      " |      Get dict of values from object corresponding to Container fields.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Parameters\n",
      " |      ----------\n",
      " |      obj : dataobject, list, tuple, or ndarray\n",
      " |          Object to get field dictionary from.\n",
      " |      *fields : str\n",
      " |          Names of corresponding fields (in self.__fields__)\n",
      " |      **fielddict\n",
      " |          Mapping of fields in obj corresponding to fields in self.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Returns\n",
      " |      -------\n",
      " |      field_dict : dict\n",
      " |          Dictionary of fields and their values.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Examples\n",
      " |      --------\n",
      " |      >>> ex = ExContainer(1.0, 2.0)\n",
      " |      >>> ex.get_field_dict([5.0])\n",
      " |      {'x': 5.0}\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      >>> ex2 = ExContainer(3.0, 4.0)\n",
      " |      >>> ex.get_field_dict(ex2)\n",
      " |      {'x': 3.0, 'y': 4.0}\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      >>> ex.get_field_dict({'x': 3.0, 'z': 40.0}, x='x', y='z')\n",
      " |      {'x': 3.0, 'y': 40.0}\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      >>> ex.get_field_dict(ex)\n",
      " |      {'x': 1.0, 'y': 2.0}\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  get_memory(self)\n",
      " |      Get approximate memory impact of dataobject and its fields.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  get_pref_attrs(self, prefix, space='_')\n",
      " |      Return dict of Container attributes with 'prefix_' as the var name.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  get_track(self, track)\n",
      " |      Get tracking params for a given dataobject (State, Mode, Rand, etc).\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Parameters\n",
      " |      ----------\n",
      " |      obj : dataobject\n",
      " |          State/Mode/Rand. Requires .default_track class variable.\n",
      " |      track : track\n",
      " |          str/tuple. Attributes to track.\n",
      " |          'all' tracks all fields\n",
      " |          'default' tracks fields defined in default_track for the dataobject\n",
      " |          'none' tracks none of the fields\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Returns\n",
      " |      -------\n",
      " |      track : tuple\n",
      " |          fields to track\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  get_true_field(self, fieldname, *args, **kwargs)\n",
      " |      Get the value that will be set to fieldname given *args and **kwargs.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  get_true_fields(self, *args, force_kwargs=False, **kwargs)\n",
      " |      Resolve the args to pass given certain defaults, *args and **kwargs.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      NOTE: must be used for pickling, since pickle passes arguments as *args and not\n",
      " |      **kwargs.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  get_typename(self)\n",
      " |      Containers are typed as containers unless specified otherwise.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  init_hist_att(self, hist, att, timerange, track, str_size='<U20')\n",
      " |      Initialize a field in the history.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  reset(self)\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  return_mutables(self)\n",
      " |      Return mutable aspects of the container.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  set_arg_type(self, *args, **kwargs)\n",
      " |      Set Parameter field input to the predetermined field type.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      e.g., if the input to parameter is int for a float field, this converts it to a\n",
      " |      float in initialization.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Parameters\n",
      " |      ----------\n",
      " |      obj : dataobject (or class)\n",
      " |          dataobject to get argument type for\n",
      " |      *args : *args\n",
      " |          args to dataobject\n",
      " |      **kwargs : **kwargs\n",
      " |          kwargs to dataobject\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Returns\n",
      " |      -------\n",
      " |      *new_args : tuple\n",
      " |          new args to dataobject (with proper type)\n",
      " |      **new_kwargs : dict\n",
      " |          new kwargs to dataobject (with proper type)\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  set_field(self, fieldname, value, as_copy=True)\n",
      " |      Set the field of the container to the given value.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Parameters\n",
      " |      ----------\n",
      " |      fieldname : str\n",
      " |          Name of the field.\n",
      " |      value : value\n",
      " |          Value to set the field to.\n",
      " |      as_copy : bool, optional\n",
      " |          Whether to copy value. The default is True.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Examples\n",
      " |      --------\n",
      " |      >>> ex_nest = ExNestContainer()\n",
      " |      >>> ex_inside = ExContainer(3.0, 4.0)\n",
      " |      >>> ex_nest.set_field('e1', ex_inside)\n",
      " |      >>> ex_nest\n",
      " |      ExNestContainer(e1=ExContainer(x=3.0, y=4.0), z=20.0)\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  to_default(self, *fieldnames)\n",
      " |      Reset given fields to their default values.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      Examples\n",
      " |      --------\n",
      " |      >>> ex = ExContainer(3.0, 4.0)\n",
      " |      >>> ex.to_default()\n",
      " |      >>> ex\n",
      " |      ExContainer(x=1.0, y=2.0)\n",
      " |\n",
      " |      >>> ex = ExContainer(4.0, 5.0)\n",
      " |      >>> ex.to_default('x')\n",
      " |      >>> ex\n",
      " |      ExContainer(x=1.0, y=5.0)\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  ----------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
      " |  Data and other attributes inherited from fmdtools.define.container.base.BaseContainer:\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  default_track = 'all'\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  rolename = 'x'\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  ----------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
      " |  Methods inherited from recordclass.datatype.dataobject:\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __copy__(self, /)\n",
      " |      T.__copy__() -- copy of T\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __eq__(self, value, /)\n",
      " |      Return self==value.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __ge__(self, value, /)\n",
      " |      Return self>=value.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __getstate__(self, /)\n",
      " |      T.__getstate__()\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __gt__(self, value, /)\n",
      " |      Return self>value.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __hash__(self, /)\n",
      " |      Return hash(self).\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __le__(self, value, /)\n",
      " |      Return self<=value.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __len__(self, /)\n",
      " |      Return len(self).\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __lt__(self, value, /)\n",
      " |      Return self<value.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __ne__(self, value, /)\n",
      " |      Return self!=value.\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __reduce__(self, /)\n",
      " |      T.__reduce__()\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __setstate__(self, object, /)\n",
      " |      T.__setstate__()\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __sizeof__(self, /)\n",
      " |      T.__sizeof__() -- size of T\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  ----------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
      " |  Static methods inherited from recordclass.datatype.dataobject:\n",
      " |\n",
      " |  __new__(*args, **kwargs) class method of recordclass.datatype.dataobject\n",
      " |      Create and return a new object.  See help(type) for accurate signature.\n",
      "\n"
     ]
    }

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "65733c0c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Simulating many scenarios\n",
    "\n",
    "The `propagate` method has a few methods available to simulate ranges of nominal parameters, faulty scenarios, and disturbances. To get a feel for how this can be used, we can use `propagate.single_faults`, which simulates all single-fault scenarios possible in a model:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 80,
   "id": "24dcf3fd",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stderr",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "SCENARIOS COMPLETE: 100%|██████████| 20/20 [00:00<00:00, 20.35it/s]\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "res_sf, hist_sf = propagate.single_faults(mdl, times=[5])"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "4b357dae",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "As shown, this pulled 20 possible faults from the model and simulated them at the specified time (t=5). We can see the structure of the results below:"

  {

   "source": [
    "## Visualizing many faults\n",
    "\n",
    "We can use the same methods (`plot_line` and `plot_trajectories`) to visualize these results"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 84,
   "id": "57f53256",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 900x400 with 6 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "fig, axs = hist_sf.plot_line(\"fxns.store_ee.s.soc\", \"fxns.plan_path.m.mode\", \"fxns.plan_path.s.dist\", \"flows.dofs.s.x\", \"flows.dofs.s.y\", \"flows.dofs.s.z\", cols=3, time_slice=[5.0])"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "53cea71d",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Grouping scenarios\n",
    "\n",
    "While comparisons of nominal and faulty can be helpful, we can further separate groups based on the `comp_groups` parameter. Here we make each scenario its own group"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 93,
   "id": "abb8e04a",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 400x400 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "fig, ax = hist_sf.plot_trajectories(\"flows.dofs.s.x\", \"flows.dofs.s.y\", \"flows.dofs.s.z\", time_groups=[\"nominal\"], comp_groups={k:k for k in hist_sf.nest()})"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "2bdf2e78",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "As shown, there are three main trajectories--crashing immediately (in grey), flying erratically (the `ctlup` fault in pink), and continuing the mission (in teal). Given this visualization, it may not be clear what scenarios ended in what outcome\n",
    "\n",
    "More parameters can be used to visualize distributions of outcomes within these groups."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "22e2491b",
   "metadata": {},
